structured_output.summary: Transit on target in 7 sectors, FPP 0.03, Rp 8.0 Re; density ratio 14 cautions.
reasons: The signal is real and periodic: it is recovered independently in every other sector searched (other_sector_results: S11 SNR 8.6, S38 7.9, S64 9.2, S65 9.8, S99 8.9, S100 7.6, all near expected SNR), and the joint_search_snr is 20.5 against joint_search_highest_null_snr 6.5. The all-sector figure shows a consistent ~3.6 h dip in all seven sectors with fit_depth_ppm 627 +/- 26.

It is new: exofop_tois, exofop_ctois and published_signal are all empty, ephemeris_match_likely_sources is empty, and the record shows no TOI, CTOI, TCE or TESS EB match in the catalogues of 2026-10-29.

The size is planetary: planet_radius_earth_radii 8.04 +/- 0.78 with fit_radius_ratio 0.0207 on a stellar_radius_solar_radii 3.546 star; transit_grazing is False and fit_impact_parameter 0.358 +/- 0.2456, so the radius is constrained and far below the 22.4 Earth-radius stellar limit.

No eclipsing-binary signatures on the target: secondary_depth_ppm 14 +/- 22 (secondary_maximum_planet_depth_ppm 12), ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm 16 +/- 23 with ellipsoidal_companion_mass_solar_masses not detected, odd_even_difference_sigma 1.26, gaia_ruwe 0.82, gaia_non_single_star 0. The ellipsoidal non-detection excludes a massive companion at 3.22 d on this 3.5-solar-radius star.

Caution 'Gaia radial velocity variable' (gaia_rv_variable True, gaia_rv_epoch_range_km_s 8.44, gaia_rv_chisq_pvalue 1.8e-15) does not refute: gaia_rv_semi_amplitude_upper_limit_km_s 4.18 gives gaia_rv_companion_mass_upper_limit_solar_masses 0.0324, so any companion at this period is below stellar mass. The RV scatter may be subgiant jitter or a longer-period companion; a spectroscopic follow-up should check it.

Caution 'stellar density does not fit the star' is the strongest warning: stellar_density_fit_to_tic_ratio 14 (fit_scaled_semi_major_axis 6.54 +/- 0.728 and fit_duration_hours 3.599 are too short for the TIC 3.55-solar-radius star). This can mean a higher impact parameter than the fit prefers (fit_impact_parameter_error 0.2456 is large), a wrong TIC radius, or a transit on a smaller blended star. It is a flag for follow-up, not a refutation.

Caution 'neighbour able to cause dip' is tied to the pixel result: pixel_verdict is 'on target' from S101 (SNR 8.5), but the S101 and joint best star (joint_best_source Gaia DR3 5861913340027287424) is the 7" G 17.5 neighbour that needs a 36% dip, and joint_pixel_verdict is 'unresolved' at joint_difference_image_snr 9.1. At 7" TESS pixels cannot separate the two stars; the S101 figure shows the difference image centred on the target pixel, consistent with either. Only ground-based seeing-limited photometry can settle this, which a CTOI submission would trigger.

I disagree with how much weight the TRICERATOPS result carries: fpp_mean 0.03024 is 'likely planet', but nfpp_mean 9.4e-24 is essentially by construction because nearby_scenarios_excluded is True, while the joint pixel verdict is unresolved. The FPP therefore understates the blend risk from the 7" neighbour; this should be stated in the submission notes.

Depth differences between sectors (depth_ppm_by_sector S11 814 +/- 72 to S100 431 +/- 68, sector_depth_consistency_p_value 0.00713) are not reproduced in the uniform-aperture cutouts (cutout_sector_depth_consistency_p_value 0.208), so they are most likely pipeline-aperture dilution differences, not a variable-depth false positive.

Holding for unreleased_tess_sectors_observing_the_star 112 113 114 would not decide the open questions: three more sectors raise the joint difference-image SNR only modestly, and 7" remains well inside a 21" pixel. The decisive data are ground-based photometry of the 7" neighbour and a spectrum of the subgiant, both of which follow from a CTOI; I therefore agree with the mechanical decision to propose for submission, with the density mismatch and unresolved neighbour flagged.
